messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: elevated p99/gpu-latency and NVMe paging on kv-cache pool 'tp-shard-42' (alerts: gpu-p99>1.2s, nvme-pageins>500/s) — severity: sev2
emily.oc: seeing the same in the dashboard, p99 for inference_gen spiked ~1.8s around 2048000000. Multiple customers showing errors 503s.
raj.runtime: looks like continuous-batching gone wild after last config deploy earlier today. I see batch window=500ms and max_batch_tokens=2e6 in the window on those shards.
sophie.sre: NVMe paging is up, hosts on gpul-45/46 showing heavy io wait. Could be cache blowup causing large memory working sets and evictions -> paging.
micaela.ml: any recent rollout of kv-shard partitioning code? we merged the tp-kv-shard-refactor last week.
raj.runtime: yeah that changed the shard sizing heuristics. hypothesis: continuous batching + new shard sizing -> too many key inserts, uneven partitioning -> some shards huge, others small. uneven tensor-parallel distribution -> NCCL all-reduce stalls when ranks wait for stragglers.
emily.oc: customer impact: CS reports 3 customers on Dedicated saw rate-limit errors and timeouts, internal traffic also degraded. tagging as Sev2 until we confirm rollback/hotfix.
kevin.prodtools: I can flip routing to fallback-capacity in the canopy region to reduce customer impact, want me to do that?
emily.oc: yes please, route all traffic for affected tenants to fallback-region-a until we have a stable mitigation. add sticky=false.
kevin.prodtools: routing change queued, will go live in 30s.
jamie-cs: notifying customers on impacted list, adding note that we're investigating and routing some traffic.
raj.runtime: immediate mitigation steps I propose: 1) disable continuous_batching on all tp-kv shards 2) reduce max_batch_tokens to safe default (200k) 3) trigger rolling restart of gpul hosts for the hot shards 4) revert the shard-sizing tweak if it's the culprit.
sophie.sre: agree on disable batching first, that should stop new inserts spiking. I can run the disable via the feature-flags service.
micaela.ml: also capture a heap/profile of kv cache entries before restart if possible, we need to understand key distribution for postmortem.
emily.oc: go for disable batching now, raj/sophie coordinate. I’ll stay on call.
raj.runtime: running: 
```bash
# disable continuous batching for tp-kv shards
curl -X POST https://config.api.internal/flags/continuous_batching/disable -d '{"scope":"tp-kv"}'
```
raj.runtime: response ok, flag rollout 100% in 12s.
sophie.sre: monitoring NVMe pageins… pageins trending down from 520/s -> 180/s after flag, p99 latency starting to fall to ~900ms.
kevin.prodtools: routing to fallback-region-a is live. customer traffic reduced on primary by ~40%.
jamie-cs: customers acknowledged. some are reporting progress, others still seeing intermittent timeouts.
micaela.ml: I captured a KV sample dump from shard-42 before restart. distributes looks skewed: shard-42 holds 3.8x the avg keys. Also noticed recent batch-append logic can append duplicate kvs under heavy concurrency.
raj.runtime: that explains blowup. duplicated inserts amplify size, continuous batching masked it by coalescing, but with weird batching window it caused runaway merge.
emily.oc: next step: rolling restarts for affected hosts to flush KV and free memory, but do safe rolling (one host at a time), notify oncall.
sophie.sre: starting restart of gpul-45 now. will watch NCCL stalls and redispatch.
raj.runtime: while restart happens, I’ll push a patch to prevent duplicate key appends in the batch merge: quick guard check in kv_merge: check-and-skip if key already present in local buffer. small patch, can hotpatch in runtime container.
raj.runtime: patch applied to gpul images on host; restarting process on gpul-45 completed. NVMe pageins down to 60/s, gpu p99 380ms, no NCCL stalls observed.
emily.oc: good. how many hosts left?
sophie.sre: restarting gpul-46 next, then gpul-47. performing healthcheck 2mins after each restart.
kevin.prodtools: also reverted batching config to safe defaults: max_batch_tokens=200000, batch_window_ms=150. snippet: 
```yaml
batching: 
  continuous: false
  max_batch_tokens: 200000
  batch_window_ms: 150
```
raj.runtime: config rollback committed. will also open an immediate PR to re-evaluate shard sizing heuristics — but that is medium-term.
micaela.ml: capturing evals for a few prompt sets to ensure quality not impacted by the batching change.
jamie-cs: customers patched, one enterprise customer requested timeline and RCA, I'll coordinate with ops and PM.
emily.oc: handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. @sophie.sre you take primary on-call, @raj.runtime you’re the engineering lead for follow-up. checklist for handoff: 1) ensure all hosts healthy 2) confirm NVMe pageins <100/s for 10m 3) verify no NCCL stall alerts 4) gather sample KV dumps for postmortem 5) coordinate RCA doc and customer comms.
sophie.sre: taking over. current status: NVMe pageins stable ~55/s, p99 latency ~320ms, no 503 errors in last 10m. continuing monitoring for 1h.
raj.runtime: next engineering tasks: 1) PR to guard duplicate inserts (merged to hotfix branch) 2) follow-up PR to replay shard sizing across simulated workload 3) implement shard rebalancer to avoid 3.8x hotspots 4) add alerting for kv-shard-key-skew >2x.
emily.oc: thanks all. will add incident notes in pagerduty and create a postmortem ticket. tagging: sev2 -> monitoring.
incident-bot: INCIDENT update: status changed to mitigated at 2048000360.
sophie.sre: leaving a quick note for next oncall: if we see p99>1s again, immediate steps: flip routing, disable batching, escalate to runtime eng, capture KV dumps, do rolling restarts.
jamie-cs: I'll send timeline + affected tenants to the customers and follow up tomorrow.
emily.oc: great work team :thumbsup: we’ll do full RCA and list corrective actions (hotfixes + alerting + sim tests).
